sentences.en: One afternoon, the sky suddenly clouded over.
Just before the end of the working day, it was already pouring outside.
Li Wen hadn't brought an umbrella, so she had to stand at the door of the building and wait for the rain to stop.
The subway station wasn't far, but in rain this heavy her clothes were sure to get wet if she walked.
"Are you going to the subway station?" a young man asked, walking over to her. "My umbrella is big, we can walk together."
Li Wen felt a little embarrassed, but the rain was getting heavier and heavier, so she said yes.
The two of them talked as they walked.
It turned out they both worked in that building; they had just never run into each other in the lift.
When they reached the station, Li Wen thanked him again and again.
The next morning, it was raining again.
This time, Li Wen ran into the man in the lift.
His hair and his clothes were wet.
"I left my umbrella at home," he said with a smile.
Li Wen took out her own umbrella and smiled too: "Never mind. Today it's my turn."

topic: Grandpa learns to use a phone

sentences.en: My grandpa is seventy-five this year.
A few days ago it was his birthday, and I bought him a new phone.
Grandpa said, "I'm old. I'll never manage to learn it."
I told him, "It's not hard. I'll teach you."
From that day on, I taught him a little every evening: how to make a call, how to send a WeChat message, how to take photos.
Grandpa studied very hard.
Every lesson, he first put on his glasses, then wrote down every step in a little notebook.
He said, "With my glasses on, the words on the phone aren't small any more."
A week later, he could already send me WeChat messages.
After that, he learned to take photos with his phone too.
Every morning when he goes to the park to exercise, he takes lots of photos of flowers and trees and sends them to everyone in the family.
His old friends who exercise with him in the park can all take photos now too, because Grandpa taught them.
Now Grandpa's phone is even busier than mine.
Yesterday I called him, and he didn't pick up.
In the evening he sent me a WeChat message: "I was in an English class online just now!"

title.en: The little dog that followed me home

sentences.en: This afternoon I saw a little white dog at the school gate.
It was very small and looked hungry.
When I walked, it walked; when I stopped, it stopped too.
I gave it a bit of bread. It ate it all up in no time, then started wagging its tail at me.
It was getting dark, and I thought: doesn't it have a home?
I picked it up in my arms and took it home.
My little brother loved it and held it in his arms the whole time.
When Mum saw it, she smiled and said, "All right, you can keep it. But you have to take it out for a walk every day."
The little dog seemed to understand, and wagged its tail again.
That night my little brother and the little dog both fell asleep early.
Now it's called Xiaobai, and it's part of our family too.

topic: A chengyu story: drawing legs on a snake

sentences.en: Long ago, in the state of Chu, a man asked some friends to his home to help him.
When the work was done, he brought out a cup of wine for them to drink.
But there was only one cup of wine, and there were several of them.
Someone said, "If we all share one cup, each of us only gets a small sip. Only one person drinking it can have his fill."
Someone else said, "Let's have a contest drawing snakes. Whoever finishes first gets the wine."
Everyone agreed, and they started drawing on the ground at once.
One man drew very fast and was the first to finish.
He picked up the wine, saw that the others were still drawing, and said proudly, "You're too slow! I've still got time to give my snake a few feet."
Holding the wine in one hand, he went on drawing feet with the other.
Before he had finished the feet, another man finished his snake.
That man took the wine from him and said, "Snakes don't have feet. What you drew isn't a snake, so this wine should be mine."
With that, he drank the wine.
Only then did the man who drew the feet understand: he had been the first to finish, but because he drew a few extra feet, he ended up with no wine at all.
Later, people came to use "drawing legs on a snake" to describe someone who does something that wasn't needed, and so makes things worse instead of better.

sentences.en: The Mid-Autumn Festival is a traditional Chinese festival, held every year in the autumn.
On the night of the festival, the moon is big and round.
To Chinese people, a round full moon is like a family all together.
So even people who live far from home go back on this day to have dinner with their families.
In the evening, people often sit outside, eating and looking at the moon.
Around the festival, schools and offices close, and railway stations are full of people going home.
The festival has another tradition: eating mooncakes.
Mooncakes are round too, with all kinds of fillings inside, some sweet and some savoury.
Before the festival, friends and colleagues often give each other mooncakes too.
There is also a famous story about the festival.
Long ago, a woman called Chang'e took a kind of medicine. Her body grew lighter and lighter, and in the end she flew up to the moon.
From then on she lived on the moon all alone, missing her family very much.
So every Mid-Autumn Festival, as people look at the big round moon, they think of this story, and they miss the family members who aren't with them.

notes.title: 又 A 又 B: both A and B

sentences.en: Today, between many Chinese cities, the high-speed train has become the first choice for a lot of people when they travel.
High-speed trains are fast and smooth.
The trains are clean and quiet.
Sitting on board, you can hardly feel the train moving, and you can read, go online or rest.
The ride is so smooth that if you put a glass of water on the table, the water hardly moves.
In the past, going to a city a bit further away often meant spending a night on the train; now, by high-speed train, you're there in half a day.
Many high-speed rail stations are next to subway stations, so you can get straight on the subway when you get off.
Buying a ticket is simple too: you can do it on your phone.
To enter the station, you just swipe your ID card.
Because it's so convenient, many young people like to take the train to another city at the weekend and come back on Sunday evening.
But during the holidays a great many people take the train and tickets are often hard to get, so it's best to buy early.
Some people say high-speed rail has brought cities closer together.

Because they work in another city.
Because the trains are quieter at the weekend.

sentences.en: In many Chinese cities you often see rows of bicycles in all kinds of colours along the roadside. These are shared bikes.
They're easy to use: scan the QR code on the bike with your phone, and the lock opens by itself.
When you get where you're going, you park the bike and lock it, and your phone shows how long you rode and how much you owe.
For people who commute every day, shared bikes solve an old problem: the stretch from the subway station to the office is a bit far to walk and too expensive by taxi, but just right by bike.
Besides, cycling is good for your health and good for the environment.
So more and more people now cycle to work.
But shared bikes have also brought some new problems.
Some people leave the bikes anywhere, even in the middle of the road, and get in the way of traffic; some bikes stay broken for a long time with nobody fixing them.
Sometimes there are so many bikes outside a subway station that people on foot can't get past.
To solve these problems, many cities have set out places where the bikes may be parked.
If you park somewhere else, some bikes won't lock, or you have to pay extra.
The companies that run the bikes also send people to check them regularly and take the broken ones away to be fixed.
So for a good idea to really make life easier for everyone, it takes new technology, and it also takes everyone choosing to follow the rules.
When you ride, be careful: don't look at your phone while cycling.
Next time you ride a shared bike, don't forget to park it properly.

defs: (links a describing word to a noun)
to share (共享单车 shared bike)
(after a verb) shut, closed (锁上 to lock)
(marks a completed action or a change)
(对…来说) for, as far as … is concerned
(对…来说) for, as far as … is concerned
and also, on top of that
to ride a bike, to cycle
to affect, to get in the way of
to arrange, to send (someone to do a job)
to pay attention to, to be careful about

notes.title: 对……来说: for, as far as … is concerned
notes.explanation: 对 + a person + 来说 at the start of a sentence says whose point of view the rest is from. 对每天上班的人来说 means "for people who commute every day".

example.zh: 对每天上班的人来说，骑车正合适。
example.pinyin: duì měi tiān shàngbān de rén lái shuō, qíchē zhèng héshì.
example.en: For people who commute every day, cycling is just right.

notes.title: Verb + 起来: when you do it
notes.explanation: 起来 after a verb can mean "when you actually do it", and is followed by your impression of it: 用起来很简单, simple to use. 听起来 (sounds) and 吃起来 (tastes) work the same way.

example.zh: 共享单车用起来很简单。
example.pinyin: gòngxiǎng dānchē yòng qǐlai hěn jiǎndān.
example.en: Shared bikes are easy to use.

questions.question: How do you unlock a shared bike?
options: With a key from the company.
By scanning the QR code with your phone.
By paying cash to a worker.

questions.question: 共享单车解决了上班的人的什么问题？
options: 从家到地铁站太远，不能走路。
从地铁站到公司的路，走路有点儿远，打车又太贵。

questions.question: Which of these is a problem the text mentions?
options: The bikes are too expensive to ride.
Some bikes are left in the middle of the road.
The QR codes often don't work.

questions.question: 作者觉得，好办法要真正方便大家，还需要什么？
options: 每个人自觉按照规定去做。
